item.title: Forgotten Authors: Arthur Leo Zagat
item.description: Last week, I mentioned Arthur Leo Zagat, who was born in New York on February 15, 1896. He collaborated with Nat Schachner on their first eleven short stories, before they both launched solo careers. Like Schachner, Zagat attended City College, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree. item.title: Forgotten Authors: F. Anstey
item.description: Thomas Anstey Guthrie was born in London on August 8, 1856. He attended King’s College School and studied at Trinity Hall in Cambridge. item.description: Charles Saunders (1946 – 2020) was one of two men who established a sub-genre of Sword & Sorcery that has come to be called Sword & Soul. The other was Samuel Delany (1942 – ). item.title: A Curious Amalgam: Joan and Peter by H.G. Wells
item.description: Science fiction fans naturally know H.G. Wells best for his scientific romances. But after 1905, he wrote relatively little in that genre. item.title: Forgotten Authors: P. Schuyler Miller
item.description: Peter Schuyler Miller was born on February 21, 1912 in Troy, New York. He earned a Master of Science from Union College and worked as a technical writer for General Electric and the Fisher Scientific Company. Miller had a lifelong interest in archaeology and was a member of the New York State Archaeological Association.
